slides.say: Triangle A B C is right at C, and C D is the altitude to A B. Given: A C is fifteen centimeters, B C is twenty centimeters, and A B is twenty-five centimeters. What is C D, in centimeters?
C D is an altitude, and an altitude always comes with an area. [short pause] So we'll find the area of the triangle in two ways, and then set them equal.

[short pause] Here's the figure again, bigger. First way, with the legs. The right angle is at C, so A C and B C are perpendicular. That means B C is the altitude to the side A C. So the area is fifteen times twenty, over two. Fifteen times twenty is three hundred, and half of that is a hundred fifty.
at: The right angle is at C
half of that is a hundred fifty

slides.say: Second way, with the side A B, which is twenty-five. The altitude to A B is the segment from C straight down to it, at a right angle. That's C D, our h. So the area is also twenty-five times C D, over two.
at: The altitude to A B is

slides.say: It's the same triangle, so it's the same area. Twenty-five times C D, over two, is a hundred fifty. So twenty-five times C D is twice that, three hundred. Three hundred divided by twenty-five is twelve, so C D is twelve. Choice number two is our answer.
at: twenty-five times C D is twice that
Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Careful with two traps. Six, choice number one, is a hundred fifty divided by twenty-five: someone forgot to double the area first. And twelve and a half, choice number three, is half of A B. That's the median to the hypotenuse, not the altitude.
at: twelve and a half, choice number three

slides: A short way to remember it, in a right triangle: one leg times the other leg equals the hypotenuse times the altitude to it. Fifteen times twenty is three hundred, and three hundred divided by twenty-five is twelve. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
